sources.author: Hooman
patch_list: Keeps the optional Microsoft cloud sign-in onboarding from replacing SwiftKey's launcher, so local keyboard setup and settings remain usable without an account. This does not sign in or unlock cloud sync and other account-backed features.

Stops SwiftKey's first-party telemetry records and uploads, Adjust attribution, Crashlytics, Firebase Sessions, legacy Google Analytics, and app exception reporting. Push messaging and the multipurpose job service stay enabled.

patch_list: Adds a local toolbar editor to SwiftKey settings. Choose and reorder shortcuts; the native Reorder items button opens it too. Choose fewer or more shortcuts; native layout distributes visible icons and More options remains available.

Keeps the optional Microsoft cloud sign-in onboarding from replacing SwiftKey's launcher, so local keyboard setup and settings remain usable without an account. This does not sign in or unlock cloud sync and other account-backed features.

Stops SwiftKey's first-party telemetry records and uploads, Adjust attribution, Crashlytics, Firebase Sessions, legacy Google Analytics, and app exception reporting. Push messaging and the multipurpose job service stay enabled.
